Subject: Supplier financial onboarding — wave 1: legal, tax & PO routing

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for this integration. We're kicking off the finance & procurement intake for ClearLine (wave 1: entity & payments). To get the vendor record created and enable PO routing + payment rails we need the items below. If you can return the documents or a short email confirming fields by EOD Wed (5/5), we can target supplier activation the following week.

Required (please attach where possible):
- Legal entity name and full remittance address (registered HQ + any additional remit-to)
- Tax form: W-9 (for US entity) — or equivalent tax residency docs if non-US
- Bank letter or ACH letterhead confirming account name, routing, account number (PDF)
- Remit instructions: preferred payment method (ACH or wire), net terms (if any), and PO acceptance email address
- Invoice examples (one PDF) and invoice email routing

Optional but helpful:
- Deloitte/CPA bank-letter if available (speeds verification)
- Any vendor code you prefer us to populate in PO description

I've attached a Redwood PO routing template and a short checklist to accelerate review. Once we receive items we'll: 1) create vendor entity, 2) provision PO routing + default payment rails, 3) confirm first PO test.

Deliver to: finance@redwood.com (or reply all to this thread).

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Procurement Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

1) ClearLine is US-registered (EIN on W-9). We can share the W-9 and a bank letter. Is a bank letter on company letterhead sufficient or do you require a voided check?
2) For PO acceptance, do you require a signed vendor acknowledgement for terms or will acceptance of the PO via the designated inbox be sufficient?

We'll prepare: W-9, bank letter (PDF), sample invoice, and confirm remit address. Targeting to send everything by end of day Tuesday (5/4).

Aisha — forwarding Samira's reply. A few notes from ops/finance: 

- Bank letter on company letterhead is acceptable if it includes account name, account number and routing. A voided check is preferred for ACH in cases where bank-letter wording is ambiguous.
- For PO routing, we prefer vendor acknowledgement for first-time vendors for legal clarity, but operationally acceptance via the finance inbox is fine if they confirm remit address and tax info.
- Markus: please confirm whether we should require vendor to sign our standard vendor payment terms (I can attach the clause).
- Rishi: once we have docs, please run the entity through our verification bucket (KYC + tax check). If anything flags, escalate to contracts@redwood.com.

Action items:
- Aisha: confirm whether we need a signed acknowledgement (Marissa left open).
- Markus: advise on payment-term requirement.
- Rishi: readiness to run verification once attachments arrive.

Thanks — I can join the kickoff call if ClearLine wants one.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference

Thanks Samira — appreciate the quick turn. Bank letter + W-9 should be fine. If you can include a PDF of a voided check that speeds ACH verification but it's not required. For the PO acceptance, we will: 

1) Create the vendor record + populate PO routing (finance@clearline.io) once docs received.
2) Send a vendor acknowledgement form for signature only if your legal team asks; otherwise acceptance via email on the first PO is okay — we'll mark the vendor as "acknowledgement-pending" in our system and follow up.
3) Rishi will kick off verification after upload — expect a status update within 48 hours.

Next steps for ClearLine (please reply all with attachments or upload to the Drive link):
- W-9 (completed) — Samira attached; thank you.
- Bank letter (PDF) — ideally on bank letterhead; voided check accepted if easier.
- Remit address confirmation (confirm if different from HQ)
- One sample invoice (PDF)

I'll loop in Contracts only if verification flags on Rishi's side. Marissa, Markus — let me know if you want the vendor acknowledgement sent automatically.

Samira — once we have the files I'll confirm vendor record creation and a test PO number.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Procurement Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
